payload.friendly_name: The CLI commits its own writes; dirty gates are Mission-scoped
payload.purpose_context: Benchmark runs and seven Mission tracers show agents hand-committing files the CLI wrote and refusing on other Missions' residue (#7545: #7556, #7555, #5938, #3933).
payload.purpose_tldr: Every spec-kitty command commits the tracked files it writes, and dirty-tree gates count only the Mission's own paths.

payload.question: When a gate that guards a Mission write sees dirt outside every Mission (for example src/ edits), does it refuse or warn?

payload.final_answer: Per #7556: record-analysis commits only its report, so dirt outside the Mission is a warning there; the single_branch implement claim keeps refusing on code dirt (the WP commits code in that checkout) and only another Mission's kitty-specs/ files become a warning. Operator absent (cloud dispatch); answer taken from the issue's Expected section.

payload.question: init on a protected branch (main) inside a git repository: commit there, or leave the files?

payload.final_answer: Commit through the existing upgrade bookkeeping committer (baseline-diff set, the one holder of the scaffold-bookkeeping capability), so init behaves like upgrade on the same branch; --no-commit opts out. Flagged for operator review in the PR. Operator absent (cloud dispatch).

payload.question: Should next also commit mission-events.jsonl when the write lands in the repository root checkout (single_branch/lanes)?

payload.final_answer: No, out of scope: #5938 is the coordination-worktree case; in the root checkout the claim gate already exempts this Mission's log and consolidate's guard does not remove that checkout. Recorded as a residual. Operator absent (cloud dispatch).

payload.wp_title: Gates count only this Mission's dirt (#7556)

setup-plan and mark-status commit their writes (#3933)
